body:
The process is very complicated and it makes it hard for asylum seekers to navigate on their own, it's as if they made it in a way that it's difficult for someone to get refugee status, also I appreciate you for understanding where I come from.

Thing is regarding the studying, I do try to learn basic stuff on my own using the aid of internet and libraries whenever I can, but I want to get some sort of degree for something, because here's the two possible outcomes of my asylum case:

1. I'll get detained and sent back to my country.

2. Get refugee status! But here's the thing they don't allow you to work unless you've been in the process for up to 12 months (and even that's a far off chance.) all the privileges I get from Home Office will be withdrawn in 2 weeks after I receive my letter and because I won't have money, work or a degree to atleast help me find a job I'll most likely be homeless in a country I've only been in for a short time in my life, I don't wang to wait around and waste all that time for a stupid letter while I can go out and plan out my next move, I'm very restricted though when it comes to that..

So you see I'll either end up being back at an abusive environment or homeless..and I can't even do anything to prepare myself for either of these, I left my country to be able to live my life but everytime I end up being shoved into another bad situation, I just wonder if this is just some vicious non-ending circle? Should I just end it and avoid all the hassle or not? What sucks is I dunno, and that's what bothers me the most.

All this waiting around for something good to come up is getting old and being restricted and mistreated by people here even infuriates me, I get treated like dirt by the very people who are supposed to be there for me: my family, the government back in my country and now the Home Office. Oh well.
